capabilities: Define named appearance themes with per-theme width, font, spacing, background and color settings
Assign themes to folders with longest-path rule matching
Toggle an e-ink mode that grayscales the workspace and removes motion and shadows
Build a dashboard from grid blocks showing vault statistics, note fields, embedded notes, GitHub files or Dataview queries
Show the active theme in the status bar and add commands for settings, dashboard and temporary e-ink mode
disambiguation: Not a theme installer or switcher; it applies its own appearance settings per folder through CSS variables rather than managing community themes.
extras: Requires Obsidian 1.13.0 or later; warns that the GitHub token is stored in plaintext in data.json and recommends a fine-grained read-only token or leaving it empty for public repositories.
problem: Obsidian themes and CSS snippets apply vault-wide, so users cannot give different folders different reading widths, backgrounds or colors without hand-written snippets.

relations.evidence: Requires the Dataview plugin; if it is missing the block says so instead of failing.
GitHub file — a file from a repository, refreshed on a schedule.

summary: Folder-scoped appearance presets that vary reading width, typography, background, transparency and e-ink mode per folder, plus a custom dashboard.
